findings: Three reader-and-congregation labels, at qadosh, barukh_kevod and yimlokh (amidah_qedushah.xml:49), are each encoded as <tei:note type="description" corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:instruction:role/reader_and_congregation" xml:lang="he"><tei:choice><tei:abbr>קו״ח</tei:abbr><tei:expan>קהל וחזן</tei:expan></tei:choice></tei:note>.
Four reader labels, at neqaddesh, leummatam, uvedivrei and ledor_vador, are still ח׳ expanded to חזן with corresp role/reader.
Both role URNs are canonical in instruction.jsonl:99-100. No reader_and_congregation label uses role/congregation.

The labels follow the 'Kinds of rubric' guidance: a label naming who says the passage is a description, placed first inside the passage it belongs to. Each note comes right after its prayer-part milestone. The previous part ends at that milestone, so the label is not left inside the part before it.
The labels follow the abbreviations guidance: the printed form is kept in tei:abbr and the editorial expansion in tei:expan, so readings.abbreviations can pick either.
No @rend appears anywhere in the file. Divine names stay in j:divineName.

The repetition and minyan guard is unchanged: the j:conditional requires both opensiddur:recitation/repetition=true and opensiddur:quorum/minyan=true under j:all. It closes with a matching j:endConditional. The heading note 'קדושה לש״ץ בחזרת התפלה.' is correctly a description, because it says both when and what.
The milestone sequence still ends with a bare prayer-part terminator after hael_haqadosh.

unit_review_text (build.py:237-245) adds abbr + ' [' + expan + ']' for each speaker segment. Both fields therefore feed the reviewed payload. The role is derived only from expan, so the role is covered too.
require_review runs before any document is built. With a changed abbr or expan, a non-draft build stops with 'Independent review pending or stale' and writes nothing.

The test at test_marmorstein_rosh_hashanah_1.py:112-145 uses speaker {abbr:'קו״ח', expan:'קהל וחזן'} and checks that it builds to role/reader_and_congregation. It then changes abbr to 'קו׳' and expan to 'קהל' one at a time. Each change must raise 'stale' and leave the output file byte-for-byte unchanged.

An unknown expansion cannot quietly become congregation. build.py:192-193 looks the expansion up in a dict with no default, so anything other than חזן, קהל or קהל וחזן fails with a KeyError. This applies in --draft mode too.

Gap: no test covers an unknown expansion. The 'קהל' subtest fails on staleness before the mapping is reached, and 'קהל' is a valid key anyway. I suggest a draft-mode test with an unmapped expansion, and replacing the bare KeyError with a ValueError that says what went wrong.
Gap: nothing checks that abbr and expan agree (for example ח׳ with קהל וחזן would build). Only human review catches that.

Related, but outside this file's code path: expanded_order (build.py:288) writes 'חזן' if role == 'reader' and 'קהל' otherwise. A section-level role of reader_and_congregation would show the text קהל while its corresp says reader_and_congregation. That is exactly a quiet fallback to congregation and should be an explicit mapping.
